stops.note: a plain word for a pillar
named the commander at the head of a regiment's 'little column' of soldiers
stops.meaning: commander of a column of troops

stops.note: borrowed from Italian with a sound change (dissimilation) that altered the first consonant
the spelling was reformed to match the Italian original, though the French-derived pronunciation persisted

current_meaning: a senior military officer rank, above lieutenant colonel and below brigadier general
